questions.question: Which contract should exist before an agent receives a refund tool?
options: Allowed actions, data scope, amount limit, and approval conditions
A promise that the model will behave
questions.explanation: Tool authority must be enforced as a machine-checkable envelope covering actions, data, limits, and approval rules.

questions.question: A tool times out after every attempt. What should a bounded runtime do?
options: Exhaust a declared retry budget, record the attempts, then stop or escalate
questions.explanation: A retry budget and explicit stop condition prevent loops and preserve an auditable outcome when the dependency remains unavailable.

questions.question: Why must an approval bind to the exact proposed arguments?
options: So a later action cannot reuse approval after its amount or target changes
So the agent can skip tool-side validation
So the trace can omit the action
questions.explanation: Approval is meaningful only for the reviewed action. Changed arguments create a different risk and require a new decision.

questions.question: A case history exceeds the context budget. Which response preserves evidence best?
options: Summarize with source pointers or stop before planning
questions.explanation: Provenance-aware compaction or an explicit stop avoids silently changing the evidence on which the agent acts.

questions.question: What makes a planner loop operationally bounded?
options: A maximum turn count plus progress detection and a stop outcome
questions.explanation: A runtime must detect repeated states and stop after a bounded number of turns rather than consuming resources indefinitely.

questions.question: An observe-only guardrail detects a $480 refund outside a $200 limit. What risk remains?
options: None, because the event was logged
The action can still execute unless a policy gate or tool blocks it
questions.explanation: Observability is not enforcement. A warning cannot prevent a side effect unless an effective gate or tool-side check rejects it.

questions.question: Which trace is most useful for auditing an agent action?
options: Task, policy decisions, tool arguments, approvals, results, timings, and stop condition
questions.explanation: An audit trace should capture observable decisions and effects without relying on private model reasoning.

questions.question: A run scores well on task completion but executes an unsafe write. Should it pass release evaluation?
options: Yes, task completion is the only metric
No, safety gates must be independently enforced rather than averaged away
Only if the tool call was expensive
questions.explanation: A critical safety failure should block release even when aggregate quality or efficiency scores look strong.
